entries.lesson_title: Definition of the Unit Step Function
entries.core_move: State the value-based definition of the unit step function and interpret it as the basic continuous-time on-off signal used to build shifted, delayed, and rectangular-pulse signal descriptions.

entries.lesson_title: Unit Step as an On-Off Switch
entries.core_move: Interpret $x(t)$$u(t)$ as using the unit step as an on-off switch that suppresses a continuous-time signal before $t = 0 and passes it afterward$, supporting construction of started, delayed, and pulsed signals with unit steps.
Translate shifted unit step functions into exact switch-on times on the continuous-time axis so they can be used to start, delay, and construct signals compactly.

entries.lesson_title: Starting a Signal with a Unit Step
entries.core_move: Convert a zero-before-start continuous-time signal from piecewise form into a step-gated expression by multiplying the active formula by the unit step that turns on at the start time.

entries.lesson_title: Delaying Exponential Signals with Unit Steps
entries.core_move: Convert a delayed exponential into the correct unit-step form e^{$a(t - t0)$}$u(t - t0)$, recognizing how the shifted step turns the signal on at t0 while the exponential's argument sets the delayed time origin.

entries.lesson_title: Building Rectangular Pulses with Unit Steps
entries.core_move: Construct rectangular pulses by subtracting appropriately shifted unit step functions to switch a chosen amplitude on at the leading edge and off at the trailing edge.
